title.en: Differences on Salvation: Orthodox vs Protestant
title.el: Διαφορές στη Σωτηρία: Ορθοδοξία vs Προτεσταντισμός
title.ru: Различия в спасении: Православие против протестантизма

content.en:
### Differences on Salvation

Protestants focus on salvation as justification: 'I can go to heaven rather than hell.' The Orthodox approach is 'maximalist': 'How can I be MOST saved?'

#### The Role of Baptism

St. John Chrysostom describes baptism not just as remission of sins, but as sanctification, justice, filial adoption, and inheritance. Everything depends on us and our zeal to keep the spiritual garment clean and spotless. It is a 'marriage', an 'enrollment in the army'.

#### Both/And vs Either/Or

Orthodoxy insists that the whole truth lies in holding on to apparently contradictory concepts: One God and Three Persons; One Person and Two Natures. On points where a Protestant wants an *either/or* answer, an Orthodox will insist on ***both/and***.

#### The Integrative Approach

The Orthodox approach to Scripture is 'integrative'. It takes the parable of the goats and sheep as seriously as Ephesians 2:8-9. Salvation includes repentance, baptism, carrying our cross, and confidence in God's mercy.
